summary: Batch governance activity observations without weakening invalidation

delivery.outcome: Resolve governance activity in one revalidated read batch, reducing repeated Git observations while preserving reservations on invalidation.
nonGoals: Changing terminal authority, ancestry policy or writer ownership
Changing required checks or the existing CI deadline
Updating adopter pins or deploying a runtime

architecture.decision: Reuse the canonical ActivityReadBatch context for the active-ticket cohort. Accept inactivity only after exit revalidation; retain every active projection with the existing diagnostic when the cohort is invalidated.
interfaceChanges: The existing governance validator path is counted as one public interface by the hub policy. Its CLI and result shape stay stable; activity inspection now revalidates one cohort before accepting inactivity.
architecture.rollback: Revert the source change through the ordinary independently validated delivery process; adopter upgrades remain separate.

validation.evidence: Nine new real-Git regressions pass. Stable 40-ticket resolution preserves results with 18 subprocesses versus 280 before batching.
Registry, target, policy and projection mutations retain all active reservations with one GOV-TICKET-ACTIVITY-001 diagnostic; unavailable inspection also remains conservative.
29 affected tests pass, including invocation isolation, reactivation, sibling changes and canonical batch invalidation. No active projections require no Git inspection.

commands: protected exact-head CI and independent Validator publication
validation.evidence: Local managed gate and affected tests are recorded; the complete diff must pass the explicit delivery contract and protected publication remains pending.
